{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-or-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"536b2e8c4d816dea13b52ba930f1d798da008d066ee9fc04b37a9bb25cc5af51","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-or-class-c:lineage:1","source_registry_sha256":"ce8335c1d96ff7ed209bf236ba9a56fe92dfebd915bc0e2fa7fb830ee03f0f09","source_liveness_sha256":"c4da479589e7933e4eef7366086dfcc48a420303d0089cb0ea19ad9137abec1d"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Testing: vision, Class C knowledge test and drive test","heading":"C — Testing: what DMV checks, the Class C knowledge test in an office or online, the drive test, test vehicle equipment and appointments","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Testing: what DMV checks, the Class C knowledge test in an office or online, the drive test, test vehicle equipment and appointments
Knowledge domain: the three tests Oregon DMV gives for an original Class C non-commercial driving privilege, the rules for sitting the knowledge test at an office or online, and what the applicant and the vehicle must bring to the drive test.

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
In Oregon you need a valid driving privilege to drive a motor vehicle on highways and on premises that are open to the public. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
The Oregon Driver Manual covers only what is needed to obtain a Class C non-commercial driving privilege. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A02
For an original driving privilege, Oregon DMV tests three things: your vision, your knowledge of driving, and your driving skill. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A02
Before each test you must pay the test fee and show proof of your identity, your date of birth and your current home address. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A02
The test fee is paid on its own, separately from any other fee you owe DMV, and most DMV offices can give the tests. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A02
If you wear glasses or contact lenses for the vision test, your driving privilege will show that you must drive with corrective lenses. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A02
The vision test is free, and an applicant who fails it is handed a form to take to a licensed vision specialist. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A03
The Class C knowledge test covers road signs, traffic laws and other things a driver must know, and the manual is meant to contain everything needed to pass it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A03
The Class C knowledge test has 35 multiple-choice questions, and you pass by answering 28 of them correctly. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A03
You can take the knowledge test online through DMV2U at any hour, or at a DMV office either as a walk-in on standby or by appointment. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A03
In an office testing area, only the people being tested and authorized translators are allowed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A03
Office knowledge tests run on a touch-screen monitor, come in several languages with or without audio, and you may bring your own earbuds or headphones. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A03
During the test you may not use a DMV manual, notes or electronic devices, though a paper foreign-language translation dictionary is allowed with permission. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A03
Talking, writing or taking notes, using a cell phone or any electronic device, or having someone else test for you all count as cheating. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A03
Anyone caught cheating fails the knowledge test and must wait 90 days before testing again. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A03
After failing a knowledge test at an office you may be able to retest the same day, depending on how much testing capacity that office has. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A03
Applicants who need a special accommodation for the knowledge test should contact their local DMV office. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A04
The online knowledge test requires a desktop or laptop with a keyboard, mouse and webcam; phones, tablets and other touchscreen devices cannot be used. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A04
The webcam takes a clear photo of you when the online test starts and random photos during it to confirm who is taking the test. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A04
An online test taker under 18 must be supervised by a proctor who is over 21, and one proctor may supervise no more than two tests in any 24-hour period. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A04
Online, you may test twice within a 24-hour period and four times in total; after the fourth attempt you must test at a DMV office. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A04
The drive test checks turning, backing, parking, lane changes, speed control, signaling, vehicle control and general driving ability, with the examiner in the front seat giving directions and reviewing the results with you afterward. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A04
DMV may waive the drive test for a new resident who surrenders an out-of-state license that is valid or has been expired for less than one year. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A04
DMV may also waive the drive test when it receives proof that you finished an ODOT-Approved Driver Education Course within the past two years. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A05
Drive tests are by appointment only, and you must bring a passenger vehicle with current registration and valid proof of insurance, or the test is rescheduled. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A05
Only you and the examiner may ride in the vehicle during the drive test, so translators, family, friends and pets must stay out. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A05
Before the drive test, remove any weapons from the vehicle, switch off electronics such as the radio and your phone, and clear objects off the dashboard and rearview mirror. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A05
After failing a drive test you must wait until the next business day to take it again. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A05
The examiner checks the test vehicle first, and a vehicle that fails the equipment check means the drive test must be rescheduled. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A05
The test vehicle must start on its own power and have working front and rear turn signals, brake lights, a horn, seatbelts and tires that are not bald or damaged. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F31 | anchor: A05
The passenger door must open and close with its handle from both inside and outside, the passenger seat must be proper, secure and reasonably clean, and the muffler must not leak excessively or make unreasonable noise. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F32 | anchor: A06
The test vehicle must display valid registration, have side view or rearview mirrors, and give both the driver and the examiner a clear view to the front, sides and rear. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F33 | anchor: A06
When the weather calls for them, the test vehicle also needs traction tires or chains, windshield wipers, headlights, taillights and a window defroster. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F34 | anchor: A06
Drive test appointments are made through DMV2U or by calling 503-945-5000, and DMV suggests booking at least three weeks before the date you want. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F35 | anchor: A06
A certified Third Party drive tester may offer quicker appointments or times DMV does not, but the cost of testing can be higher. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F36 | anchor: A06
An applicant under 18 who is applying for a driver license must have held a permit for at least 6 months. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0013]

Misconceptions: passing the knowledge test is not the whole job, because DMV also tests vision and driving skill for an original privilege; the online test is not unlimited, since it caps attempts and then sends you to an office; a family member or translator cannot ride along on the drive test; a car that fails the equipment check ends the appointment before any driving is graded.
Mnemonics: Vision, Knowledge, Skill is the order of the three tests; pay, prove, then test describes every visit; bring a car that Starts, Signals, Stops and Sounds its horn.
Glossary: driving privilege means the legal permission to drive, issued as a permit or license; Class C means the non-commercial driving privilege this manual covers; standby service means testing at an office without an appointment; proctor means the adult who supervises a minor's online test; Third Party Tester means a certified business that gives drive tests outside DMV offices.
Dynamic facts: test fees, office hours, the DMV online service portal, the scheduling phone line and the Third Party Tester listing can change; confirm them on the Oregon DMV website.
